claims.claim: Mice lacking COL17 exhibit a premature aged skin phenotype, including gray hair and hair loss.
claims.source: Recently, COL17 has been shown to form a niche for hair follicle stem cells (HFSCs), as mice lacking the protein and human JEB patients with mutations in COL17A1, the open-reading frame encoding COL17, exhibit a premature aged skin phenotype, including gray hair and hair loss (Matsumura et al., 2016; Nishie et al., 2007; Tanimura et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Human JEB patients with mutations in COL17A1 exhibit a premature aged skin phenotype, including gray hair and hair loss.
claims.source: Recently, COL17 has been shown to form a niche for hair follicle stem cells (HFSCs), as mice lacking the protein and human JEB patients with mutations in COL17A1, the open-reading frame encoding COL17, exhibit a premature aged skin phenotype, including gray hair and hair loss (Matsumura et al., 2016; Nishie et al., 2007; Tanimura et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Reduced labeling of epidermal basement membrane proteins, including COL17, in human skin has been associated with aging.
claims.source: Additionally, reduced labeling of epidermal basement membrane proteins, including COL17, in human skin has been associated with aging (Langton et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Neonatal IFE skin (P1, postnatal day 1) of Col17a1−/− mice showed transient epidermal hyperproliferation.
claims.source: Neonatal IFE skin (P1, postnatal day 1) of Col17a1−/− mice showed transient epidermal hyperproliferation, as demonstrated by counting the epidermal layers and the numbers of epidermal cells and phospho-Histone H3 (PH3)-positive cells (Figure 1a–b).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1a-b.

claims.claim: The numbers of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA)- and Bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU)-positive cells in the Col17a1−/− IFE basal cells at P1 were increased compared with the controls.
claims.source: The numbers of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA)- and Bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU)-positive cells in the Col17a1−/− IFE basal cells at P1 were also increased compared with the controls (Figure 1c), indicating that COL17 deletion affects both the S and M phases in the cell cycle of IFE neonatal keratinocytes.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1c.

claims.claim: COL17 deletion affects both the S and M phases in the cell cycle of IFE neonatal keratinocytes.
claims.source: The numbers of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA)- and Bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU)-positive cells in the Col17a1−/− IFE basal cells at P1 were also increased compared with the controls (Figure 1c), indicating that COL17 deletion affects both the S and M phases in the cell cycle of IFE neonatal keratinocytes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the PCNA and BrdU data.

claims.claim: The proliferative IFE phenotype of Col17a1−/− mice gradually waned postnatally, and the epidermal thickness and the number of PH3-positive cells became comparable with those of the controls at P20.
claims.source: The proliferative IFE phenotype of Col17a1−/− mice gradually waned postnatally, and the epidermal thickness and the number of PH3-positive cells became comparable with those of the controls at P20 (Figure 1a–b).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1a-b.

claims.claim: The gene expression of Itga6 was increased in Col17a1−/− IFE skin.
claims.source: The gene expression of Itga6, which might compensate for COL17 deficiency, was increased in Col17a1−/− IFE skin, whereas the expression of Itgb1, itgb4, lamb3 and lamc2 was not altered (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1d.

claims.claim: The expression of Itgb1, itgb4, lamb3 and lamc2 was not altered in Col17a1−/− IFE skin.
claims.source: The gene expression of Itga6, which might compensate for COL17 deficiency, was increased in Col17a1−/− IFE skin, whereas the expression of Itgb1, itgb4, lamb3 and lamc2 was not altered (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: The mRNA expression levels of Tgm1, Ppl and Ivl were somewhat higher in Col17a1−/− IFE skin.
claims.source: The mRNA expression levels of Tgm1, Ppl and Ivl were somewhat higher in Col17a1−/− IFE skin (Figure 1d), while loricrin-labeled granular cell layers were not expanded in these mice (Figure 1e).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1d.

claims.claim: Loricrin-labeled granular cell layers were not expanded in Col17a1−/− mice.
claims.source: The mRNA expression levels of Tgm1, Ppl and Ivl were somewhat higher in Col17a1−/− IFE skin (Figure 1d), while loricrin-labeled granular cell layers were not expanded in these mice (Figure 1e).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1e.

claims.claim: Dye-permeability and transepidermal water loss at day 18.5 of embryogenesis (E18.5) were comparable between the Col17a1−/− mice and the controls.
claims.source: Dye-permeability and transepidermal water loss at day 18.5 of embryogenesis (E18.5) were comparable between the Col17a1−/− mice and the controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–c), indicating that IFE keratinocyte differentiation was not greatly altered in Col17a1−/− skin.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b-c.

claims.claim: IFE keratinocyte differentiation was not greatly altered in Col17a1−/− skin.
claims.source: Dye-permeability and transepidermal water loss at day 18.5 of embryogenesis (E18.5) were comparable between the Col17a1−/− mice and the controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–c), indicating that IFE keratinocyte differentiation was not greatly altered in Col17a1−/− skin.
claims.evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the dye-permeability and TEWL data.

claims.claim: There was no increase in the number of cells positive for cleaved caspase-3, a marker of apoptosis, in the Col17a1−/− epidermis compared with the controls.
claims.source: There was no increase in the number of cells positive for cleaved caspase-3, a marker of apoptosis, in the Col17a1−/− epidermis compared with the controls (Figure 1e).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1e.

claims.claim: The dermo-epidermal junction of the Col17a1−/− IFE presented hypoplastic hemidesmosomes.
claims.source: The electron microscopy results indicated that the dermo-epidermal junction of the Col17a1−/− IFE presented hypoplastic hemidesmosomes in accordance with previous observations on the back skin of Col17a1−/− mice (Nishie et al., 2007) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1d.

claims.claim: There were no significant differences in the number of inflammatory infiltrates, including CD3+, F4/80+ and Ly-6G+ cells, in the dermis of Col17a1−/− mice and control mice.
claims.source: There were no significant differences in the number of inflammatory infiltrates, including CD3+, F4/80+ and Ly-6G+ cells, in the dermis of Col17a1−/− mice and control mice, which excludes inflammation as a contributor to immature hemidesmosome formation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e–g).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1e-g.

claims.claim: Inflammation is excluded as a contributor to immature hemidesmosome formation in Col17a1−/− mice.
claims.source: There were no significant differences in the number of inflammatory infiltrates, including CD3+, F4/80+ and Ly-6G+ cells, in the dermis of Col17a1−/− mice and control mice, which excludes inflammation as a contributor to immature hemidesmosome formation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e–g).
claims.evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the inflammatory cell data.

claims.claim: An in silico model recapitulated the transient epidermal hyperproliferation of the Col17a1−/− neonatal IFE upon the loosening of the attachment of committed progenitor cells to the BMZ.
claims.source: To explain the transient epidermal hyperproliferation of the Col17a1−/− neonatal IFE, we exploited an in silico model (Kobayashi et al., 2016) to recapitulate the epidermal development. As COL17 serves as a linker between the epidermis and dermis and is expressed in basal cells, most of which are committed progenitor cells in the epidermis (Doupé and Jones, 2012; Lim et al., 2013), epidermal thickness was calculated upon the loosening of the attachment of committed progenitor cells to the BMZ. In the model with diminished adhesion, the epidermal thickness was transiently increased and gradually returned to the baseline (Figure 1f), which was compatible with the experimental observations of Col17a1−/− neonates and with the transient hypertrophy of Itga6- and Itgb1-null epidermis (Brakebusch et al., 2000; Niculescu et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by in silico modeling data shown in Figure 1f.

claims.claim: COL17 deletion induces epidermal thickening by the hyperproliferation of IFE keratinocytes, at least partially through the loosening of dermo-epidermal adhesion at the neonatal stage.
claims.source: These data suggest that COL17 deletion induces epidermal thickening by the hyperproliferation of IFE keratinocytes, at least partially through the loosening of dermo-epidermal adhesion at the neonatal stage.
claims.evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the in silico modeling and experimental data.

claims.claim: The cell proliferation rates of NHEKs treated with COL17A1 siRNAs were slightly decreased.
claims.source: The cell proliferation rates of NHEKs treated with COL17A1 siRNAs were slightly decreased (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b–d), which is compatible with reduced proliferation of cultured keratinocytes derived from Col17a1−/− mice (Tanimura et al., 2011), and the colony-forming abilities of these cells were similar to those of control cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2e–f).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2b-d.

claims.claim: The colony-forming abilities of NHEKs treated with COL17A1 siRNAs were similar to those of control cells.
claims.source: The cell proliferation rates of NHEKs treated with COL17A1 siRNAs were slightly decreased (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b–d), which is compatible with reduced proliferation of cultured keratinocytes derived from Col17a1−/− mice (Tanimura et al., 2011), and the colony-forming abilities of these cells were similar to those of control cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2e–f).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2e-f.

claims.claim: The proliferation potential of Col17a1−/− IFE is dependent on in vivo conditions.
claims.source: These data indicate that the proliferation potential of Col17a1−/− IFE is dependent on in vivo conditions.
claims.evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the in vitro and in vivo data.

claims.claim: The expression levels of Wnt-related molecules (Fzd4, Nfatc2, Nfatc4 and Tcf7) were significantly decreased in Col17a1−/− neonatal IFE skin compared with controls.
claims.source: The screening data showed that the expression levels of Wnt-related molecules (Fzd4, Nfatc2, Nfatc4 and Tcf7) were significantly decreased in Col17a1−/− neonatal IFE skin compared with controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by qPCR screening data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: The TGF-β and p-Smad2 immunostaining in Col17a1−/− IFE keratinocytes was comparable with that in IFE cells in the controls.
claims.source: Although the expression of some TGF-β−related genes was altered in Col17a1−/− IFE skin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a), the TGF-β and p-Smad2 immunostaining in Col17a1−/− IFE keratinocytes was comparable with that in IFE cells in the controls, in contrast to the TGF-β and p-Smad2 reduction in Col17a1−/− HFSCs (Tanimura et al., 2011) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b–c).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1b-c.

claims.claim: The expression levels of the Wnt target genes (Tcf7l1, Tcf7l2, and Axin2), the receptor gene (Fzd4), and stimulatory Wnt genes (Wnt2, Wnt2b, Wnt5a) were significantly downregulated in Col17a1−/− mice.
claims.source: In line with the screening qPCR data, the expression levels of the Wnt target genes (Tcf7 l1, Tcf7 l2, and Axin2), the receptor gene (Fzd4), and stimulatory Wnt genes (Wnt2, Wnt2b, Wnt5a) were significantly downregulated in Col17a1−/−mice, whereas expression of the inhibitory Wnt gene (Wnt4) was increased (Figure 2a) (Bernard et al., 2008; Mikels and Nusse, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2a.

claims.claim: Expression of the inhibitory Wnt gene (Wnt4) was increased in Col17a1−/− mice.
claims.source: In line with the screening qPCR data, the expression levels of the Wnt target genes (Tcf7 l1, Tcf7 l2, and Axin2), the receptor gene (Fzd4), and stimulatory Wnt genes (Wnt2, Wnt2b, Wnt5a) were significantly downregulated in Col17a1−/−mice, whereas expression of the inhibitory Wnt gene (Wnt4) was increased (Figure 2a) (Bernard et al., 2008; Mikels and Nusse, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2a.

claims.claim: The number of basal cells positive for LEF1, a nuclear Wnt mediator of Wnt signaling, was reduced in neonatal Col17a1−/− mice IFE.
claims.source: The changes in these genes were paralleled by a reduction of basal cells positive for LEF1, a nuclear Wnt mediator of Wnt signaling, in neonatal Col17a1−/− mice IFE (Figure 2b).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2b.

claims.claim: The reduction in LEF1-positive basal cells was transient, and the number of LEF1-positive basal cells was comparable between the Col17a1−/− mice and the control mice at P4.
claims.source: This reduction was also transient, and the number of LEF1-positive basal cells was comparable between the Col17a1−/− mice and the control mice at P4, which might account for the transient epidermal hyperproliferation of the paw IFE in Col17a1−/− mice.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2b.

claims.claim: The number of nuclear β-catenin-positive cells in Col17a1−/− mice IFE was diminished compared to the controls.
claims.source: As β-catenin binds to LEF1 in the nucleus in the Wnt-canonical pathway (Lien and Fuchs, 2014), we performed β-catenin immunostaining. The number of nuclear β-catenin-positive cells in Col17a1−/− mice IFE was diminished compared to the controls (Figure 2c).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: Overexpression of human COL17 significantly upregulated Wnt activity in STF293 reporter cells.
claims.source: To further evaluate the relationship between Wnt signaling and COL17, we utilized SuperTopFlash 293 (STF293) reporter cells (Tsukiyama et al., 2015). Overexpression of human COL17 significantly upregulated Wnt activity in this cell line (Figure 2d).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 2d.

claims.claim: The LacZ-positive area that was indicative of active Wnt signaling in the IFE was significantly diminished in the ins-Topgal+:Col17a1−/− mice.
claims.source: Additionally, to visualize Wnt signaling in vivo, we crossed ins-Topgal+ mice (Moriyama et al., 2007) with Col17a1−/− mice. The LacZ-positive area that was indicative of active Wnt signaling in the IFE was significantly diminished in the ins-Topgal+:Col17a1−/− mice (Figure 2e, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by LacZ staining data shown in Figure 2e and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: COL17 expression stabilizes Wnt signaling.
claims.source: These results suggest that COL17 expression stabilizes Wnt signaling.
claims.evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the reporter assay and in vivo Wnt signaling data.

claims.claim: In JEB epidermis, the numbers of LEF1-positive cells and cells with nuclear β-catenin were decreased, while the number of PH3-positive cells was elevated.
claims.source: To examine whether these findings correlate with the phenotype of JEB patients with COL17 deficiency, we also performed immunostainings for LEF1, β-catenin and PH3 in JEB skin. In the JEB epidermis, the numbers of LEF1-positive cells and cells with nuclear β-catenin were decreased, while the number of PH3-positive cells was elevated (Figure 2—figure supplement 3); these findings were compatible with the data from the Col17a1−/− mice, although this result requires further investigation due to the small sample size.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Neonatal K14-deltaNLef1 mice IFE exhibited epidermal thickening and a larger number of PH3-positive basal cells than the controls.
claims.source: K14-deltaNLef1 mice express a Lef1 transgene that lacks a β-catenin-binding site under the control of the keratin 14 (K14) promoter and serve as a model of inactive Wnt signaling in the epidermis (Niemann et al., 2002). Neonatal K14-deltaNLef1 mice IFE exhibited epidermal thickening and a larger number of PH3-positive basal cells than the controls (Figure 2f).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by histological data shown in Figure 2f.

claims.claim: The number of BrdU- and PH3-positive epidermal cells was increased in mice treated with Wnt inhibitors (IWP-2 or Wnt-C59) at P1 compared with untreated control mice.
claims.source: To confirm that the abated Wnt activities were related to neonatal IFE proliferation in vivo, we intraperitoneally administered Wnt inhibitors (IWP-2 or Wnt-C59) into wild-type mouse neonates (Kuo et al., 2016; Carotenuto et al., 2017). The number of BrdU- and PH3-positive epidermal cells was increased in mice treated with these inhibitors at P1 compared with untreated control mice (Figure 2g).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2g.

claims.claim: Transgenic rescue by the expression of human COL17 under the K14 promoter in Col17a1−/− mice abrogated IFE hyperproliferation and restored LEF1- and nuclear β-catenin-positive basal cells.
claims.source: Transgenic rescue by the expression of human COL17 (hCOL17) under the K14 promoter in Col17a1−/− mice (Nishie et al., 2007) abrogated IFE hyperproliferation and restored LEF1- and nuclear β-catenin-positive basal cells (Figure 3a,c–d).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3a, c-d.

claims.claim: The expression levels of Wnt-related genes that were altered in Col17a1−/− mice at P1 were restored by transgenic rescue with hCOL17.
claims.source: The expression levels of Wnt-related genes that were altered in Col17a1−/− mice at P1 were restored by transgenic rescue with hCOL17 (Figure 3b).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3b.

claims.claim: COL17 unambiguously contributes to the maintenance of neonatal IFE proliferation via its effect on Wnt signaling.
claims.source: These data demonstrate that COL17 unambiguously contributes to the maintenance of neonatal IFE proliferation via its effect on Wnt signaling.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the transgenic rescue data.

claims.claim: In the IFE of aged mice, the epidermis was thickened, and the numbers of PH3-, BrdU- and PCNA-positive cells were increased.
claims.source: We compared wild-type (WT) young mice (6 to 10 weeks old) with aged mice (19 to 27 months old). In the IFE of aged mice, the epidermis was thickened, and the numbers of PH3-, BrdU- and PCNA-positive cells were increased (Figure 4a).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by histological data shown in Figure 4a.

claims.claim: Physical aging leads to paw IFE hyperproliferation.
claims.source: This phenomenon was specific to paw skin and was not observed in the back skin IFE (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), as was the case for the neonatal Col17a1−/− IFE. These data indicate that physical aging leads to paw IFE hyperproliferation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the aged mouse data.

claims.claim: The gene expression levels of Itga6 and Itgb1 were decreased in the aged mouse IFE.
claims.source: The gene expression levels of Itga6 and Itgb1 were decreased in the aged mouse IFE, whereas that of Col17a1 did not change (Figure 4b).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4b.

claims.claim: The gene expression level of Col17a1 did not change in the aged mouse IFE.
claims.source: The gene expression levels of Itga6 and Itgb1 were decreased in the aged mouse IFE, whereas that of Col17a1 did not change (Figure 4b).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4b.

claims.claim: The expression levels of differentiation markers (Tgm1, Ppl, and Evpl) were not greatly affected in aged mouse IFE.
claims.source: Furthermore, the expression levels of differentiation markers (Tgm1, Ppl, and Evpl) were not greatly affected.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results.

claims.claim: The distribution of COL17 was dramatically altered in the IFE of aged mice and humans.
claims.source: Although Col17a1 gene expression was unaffected, the distribution of COL17 was dramatically altered in the IFE of aged mice and humans.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results.

claims.claim: The apico-lateral portion of COL17 (non-hemidesmosomal COL17) was greatly reduced in the IFE of aged mice and humans.
claims.source: The apico-lateral portion of COL17 (non-hemidesmosomal COL17) was greatly reduced in the IFE of aged mice and humans, as detected with antibodies targeting the extracellular portion of COL17 (Figure 4c) and is in line with the recent publication on age-related alterations of COL17 in human skin (Langton et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4c.

claims.claim: The altered COL17 distribution in aged IFE was also observed in the IFE of Klotho−/− mice, a premature aging model.
claims.source: This phenomenon was also observed in the IFE of Klotho−/− mice, a premature aging model (Kuro-o, 2008).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4c.

claims.claim: The involvement of COL17 proteolytic cleavage (ectodomain shedding) in the altered COL17 distribution was excluded.
claims.source: The involvement of COL17 proteolytic cleavage, so-called ectodomain shedding (Nishie et al., 2012, 2015), in the altered COL17 distribution was excluded using several antibodies that recognize the intracellular portions of COL17 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Triton X-100-treated young IFE lost the apico-lateral portion of COL17 and resembled the aged epidermis.
claims.source: To confirm the depletion of non-hemidesmosomal COL17 in the aged IFE, the sections were treated with Triton X-100 prior to immunostaining (Hirako et al., 1998). In both mouse and human skin, Triton X-100-treated young IFE lost the apico-lateral portion of COL17 and resembled the aged epidermis (Figure 4d).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: In 3D-reconstructed images, COL17 was confined to the basement membrane in the aged IFE, while basal cells of young mice had COL17 that was associated with the apical, lateral and basal membranes.
claims.source: To further examine the reduction in the apico-lateral portion of COL17 in aged mice, we performed whole-mount staining of the IFE (Figure 4e). In 3D-reconstructed images, COL17 was confined to the basement membrane in the aged IFE, while basal cells of young mice had COL17 that was associated with the apical, lateral and basal membranes.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by 3D imaging data shown in Figure 4e.

claims.claim: COL17 was detected at the apico-lateral cell periphery of basal keratinocytes but did not co-localize with desmosomal proteins (desmogleins 1 and 2).
claims.source: Using high-resolution structured illumination microscopy (SIM) imaging on young WT mouse IFE (Figure 4f), COL17 was detected at the apico-lateral cell periphery of basal keratinocytes but did not co-localize with desmosomal proteins (desmogleins 1 and 2), indicating that the apico-lateral COL17 in basal keratinocytes was not incorporated into desmosomes, which are highly insoluble.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by SIM imaging data shown in Figure 4f.

claims.claim: The apico-lateral COL17 in basal keratinocytes was not incorporated into desmosomes.
claims.source: Using high-resolution structured illumination microscopy (SIM) imaging on young WT mouse IFE (Figure 4f), COL17 was detected at the apico-lateral cell periphery of basal keratinocytes but did not co-localize with desmosomal proteins (desmogleins 1 and 2), indicating that the apico-lateral COL17 in basal keratinocytes was not incorporated into desmosomes, which are highly insoluble.
claims.evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the SIM imaging data.

claims.claim: The distributions of integrins α6 and β1 were not modified by aging.
claims.source: In contrast to COL17 dynamics with aging, the distributions of integrins α6 and β1 were not modified by aging (Figure 4—figure supplement 4a).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4a.

claims.claim: Other hemidesmosomal proteins (BP230 and Plectin) were unchanged with aging.

results.result: COL17 deficiency leads to transient epidermal hyperproliferation in neonatal paw IFE. Col17a1−/− mice at P1 showed increased epidermal layers, cell counts, and proliferation markers (PH3, PCNA, BrdU), which normalized by P20. This phenotype was attributed to loosened dermo-epidermal adhesion, supported by in silico modeling and hypoplastic hemidesmosomes, without major changes in differentiation or apoptosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C43 provide converging evidence from histology (C28, C31), proliferation markers (C29, C30), electron microscopy (C39), and computational modeling (C42, C43). The transient nature is well-documented (C31), and alternative explanations like inflammation (C40-C41) and differentiation defects (C36-C37) are appropriately excluded. The in silico model (C42) provides mechanistic support consistent with experimental observations.

results.result: In vitro COL17 knockdown in NHEKs slightly decreased proliferation and did not affect colony-forming ability, contrasting with the in vivo hyperproliferation phenotype. This indicates that the proliferative effects of COL17 deficiency are dependent on in vivo conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C47 demonstrate a clear distinction between in vitro and in vivo phenotypes, supported by cell proliferation assays (C45) and colony formation assays (C46). The conclusion (C47) is appropriately cautious and acknowledges the context-dependency of COL17's role in proliferation.

results.result: COL17 deficiency in neonatal IFE leads to reduced Wnt signaling. Multiple Wnt-related genes were downregulated (C48, C50, C51), LEF1-positive and nuclear β-catenin-positive cells were reduced (C52, C53, C54), and Wnt reporter activity was diminished (C55, C56). Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of Wnt signaling recapitulated the hyperproliferative phenotype (C59, C60), and similar findings were observed in JEB patients (C58).
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C60 provide comprehensive evidence linking COL17 deficiency to reduced Wnt signaling through gene expression (C48, C50-C51), protein localization (C52-C54), reporter assays (C55-C56), and genetic/pharmacological validation (C59-C60). The transient nature of LEF1 reduction (C53) correlates with the transient hyperproliferation phenotype. Human JEB data (C58) supports translational relevance, though sample size is acknowledged as limited.

results.result: Transgenic rescue with human COL17 in Col17a1−/− mice reversed neonatal IFE hyperproliferation and restored Wnt signaling. Expression of hCOL17 under the K14 promoter normalized proliferation markers, LEF1-positive cells, nuclear β-catenin, and Wnt-related gene expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C63 provide strong rescue evidence demonstrating causality. The restoration of both proliferation (C61) and Wnt signaling markers (C61, C62) upon COL17 reintroduction directly supports the conclusion (C63) that COL17 regulates neonatal IFE proliferation via Wnt signaling. This is a critical validation of the proposed mechanism.

results.result: Physical aging induces paw IFE hyperproliferation in wild-type mice. Aged mice (19-27 months) showed increased epidermal thickness and proliferation markers (PH3, BrdU, PCNA) compared to young mice (6-10 weeks). This was specific to paw skin and not observed in back skin. Gene expression of Itga6 and Itgb1 decreased with aging, while Col17a1 expression remained unchanged.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C68 establish age-related IFE hyperproliferation with multiple proliferation markers (C64), site-specificity (C65), and gene expression changes (C66-C68). The maintained Col17a1 expression (C67) despite altered protein distribution (addressed in other claims) suggests post-translational regulation. The evidence is consistent and well-controlled.

results.result: Aging dramatically alters COL17 distribution in IFE through post-translational mechanisms. The apico-lateral (non-hemidesmosomal) COL17 was greatly reduced in aged mouse and human IFE, while hemidesmosomal COL17 remained. This was confirmed by Triton X-100 treatment, 3D imaging, and high-resolution microscopy. Ectodomain shedding was excluded, and other basement membrane proteins were unchanged. Col17a1 gene expression was maintained despite protein redistribution.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C80 provide comprehensive characterization of age-related COL17 redistribution using multiple complementary techniques: immunostaining (C70), detergent extraction (C73), 3D reconstruction (C74), and super-resolution microscopy (C75-C76). The exclusion of ectodomain shedding (C72) and unchanged expression of other BMZ proteins (C77-C79) strengthens the specificity of the finding. The conclusion of post-translational regulation (C80) is well-supported.

results.result: Aging-induced alteration of aPKC contributes to COL17 redistribution in IFE. EDTA treatment mimicked aged COL17 distribution, phospho-aPKC was reduced in aged IFE, and asymmetric cell division increased with aging. Pharmacological inhibition of aPKC (Go6983, myr PSI) diminished apico-lateral COL17 in young mouse IFE and human 3D epidermis.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C87 establish a mechanistic link between aPKC and COL17 distribution through ex vivo manipulation (C81, C85-C86), in vivo observation (C83-C84), and 3D culture validation (C86). The EDTA treatment (C81) provides indirect evidence for calcium/aPKC involvement, though EDTA is not specific to calcium. The pharmacological approach (C85-C86) is appropriately validated in multiple systems. The conclusion (C87) is supported but acknowledges the limitation of potential non-specific drug effects in the discussion.

results.result: Proteases do not play major roles in age-related loss of apico-lateral COL17. Expression of COL17-degrading proteases (ADAM9/10/17, MMP9, ELANE) was unchanged with aging. MMP9 involvement was excluded using Serpine1−/− mice, and ELANE distribution was unaffected by aging.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C92 systematically exclude protease-mediated mechanisms through gene expression analysis (C88), genetic models (C89), and protein localization (C90-C91). The conclusion (C92) is appropriately cautious ('may not play major roles'). This negative result strengthens the aPKC-mediated mechanism by ruling out alternative explanations.

results.result: Overexpression of human COL17 in aged mice suppresses IFE hyperproliferation. K14-hCOL17 transgenic mice maintained COL17 on all basal cell surfaces at >19 months and showed reduced epidermal thickness and proliferation markers compared to aged wild-type mice. Itga6 and Itgb1 expression remained similar to controls, suggesting COL17 acts downstream of these stem cell markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C96 demonstrate that COL17 overexpression can reverse age-related IFE hyperproliferation. The maintained COL17 distribution (C93) and reduced proliferation (C94) provide strong evidence. The unchanged integrin expression (C95) and the inference about COL17's position in the regulatory hierarchy (C96) are appropriately presented as suggestive rather than definitive. This is a key therapeutic proof-of-concept result.

results.result: Premature aged Col17a1−/− mice (3 months) show epidermal thickening with increased BrdU-positive cells but comparable PCNA/PH3-positive cells to controls. Unlike neonatal IFE, Wnt-related molecules were not obviously altered in young adult Col17a1−/− IFE.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C99 establish that COL17 deficiency causes age-related IFE changes even in young adult mice, but through a mechanism distinct from neonatal hyperproliferation. The differential proliferation marker results (C97-C98) and absence of Wnt alterations (C99) support the conclusion that COL17 regulates IFE proliferation through distinct mechanisms at different life stages. This is consistent with the overall narrative.

results.result: Background on COL17 structure, function, and disease associations. COL17 is a transmembrane protein at the basement membrane zone, deficiency causes premature aging phenotypes and junctional epidermolysis bullosa, and it forms a niche for hair follicle stem cells. Reduced COL17 labeling is associated with aging in human skin.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C19-C27 provide established background knowledge supported by citations. These are literature-based claims that contextualize the study but do not represent novel findings from this work.

results.result: Background on IFE stem cells and aging. IFE stem cells reside in the basal layer, self-renew, and generate differentiated layers. The influence of aging on IFE proliferation has been controversial, with some studies showing decreased and others showing increased proliferation.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C18 provide literature-based background on IFE biology and the controversy regarding age-related proliferation changes. These are appropriately cited and contextualize the study's contribution to resolving this controversy.

results.result: Summary claims and conclusions. COL17 plays a central role in regulating IFE proliferation through distinct mechanisms in neonatal (via Wnt signaling) and aged skin (via aPKC-mediated distribution changes). COL17 could be an important target for anti-aging strategies.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C10, C101-C103 represent high-level summaries and conclusions drawn from the experimental results. These are well-supported by the detailed findings in other claim groups. The therapeutic speculation (C10) is appropriately presented as a possibility rather than a proven application.
